description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian curry renowned for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered in a subtly spiced gravy, creating a dish that is both comforting and exquisitely flavorful. This classic recipe promises an authentic taste of India, perfect for a memorable meal.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 mins

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1/2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, reduce heat to medium and add another tablespoon of butter. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they turn translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer and Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Add the tomato puree, remaining 1/2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala, and sugar. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomato mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate. Add the soaked cashews (drained) and 1/2 cup water or broth. Bring to a simmer, then carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Strain the gravy back into the pan for an extra silky texture, if desired.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Finish
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken to the smooth gravy. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and the crushed Kasuri Methi. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to cook through and absorb the flavors of the gravy. If the gravy is too thick, add a little more water or broth to reach your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Garnish
instructions.text: Stir in the fresh cream and adjust salt to taste. Cook for just 1-2 minutes more, ensuring the cream is fully incorporated but do not boil after adding cream. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander before serving. Serve hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the marinated chicken slightly under a broiler or on a grill before adding it to the gravy.
Always use good quality Kashmiri red chili powder for that vibrant red color without excessive heat. Soaking cashews is crucial for a smooth, rich gravy.
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
article:
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's known in its native India, is a dish that has captivated palates worldwide. Its rich, creamy texture, delicately spiced tomato gravy, and succulent pieces of chicken make it a perennial favorite on Indian restaurant menus and a highly sought-after recipe for home cooks. If you're looking to recreate this iconic dish, you've come to the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the classic Butter Chicken Recipe, ensuring you achieve that authentic, mouth-watering flavor right in your own kitchen.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken is a culinary masterpiece that originated in Delhi, India, in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its essence. It features tender pieces of chicken, traditionally cooked in a tandoor (clay oven) but easily adapted for home cooking, immersed in a velvety smooth, tomato-based sauce. The sauce is a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, enriched with butter, cream, and a medley of aromatic spices. What sets Butter Chicken apart is its balanced profile – it’s mildly spiced, making it universally appealing, yet deeply flavorful, with a comforting warmth that lingers on the palate.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

To embark on your journey to master this classic Butter Chicken Recipe, gathering the right ingredients is key. Quality components will elevate your dish from good to exceptional.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

**For the Makhani Gravy:**
*   2 tablespoons ghee or unsalted butter
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 2 cups fresh tomato puree
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional but recommended for creaminess)
*   2-3 green cardamom pods
*   1-2 cloves
*   1 small bay leaf
*   1 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to heat preference)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances tomato acidity)
*   1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, extra for finishing
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed
*   Fresh coriander leaves for garnish

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step Instructions

Creating this delightful Butter Chicken Recipe involves a few stages, but each step is straightforward and contributes to the final, exquisite flavor.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or oil in a large skillet or pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. The chicken doesn't need to be fully cooked at this stage as it will simmer in the gravy. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, add the remaining ghee or butter. Once melted, add the cardamom pods, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
4.  **Build the Flavor:** Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the crushed tomatoes (or puree), soaked cashews (drained), cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix well. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate from the mixture.
5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully remove the bay leaf, cardamom pods, and cloves (if you can find them easily). Transfer the cooked mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an ultra-silky, restaurant-quality texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  **Simmer and Combine:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add a splash of water or chicken broth if the gravy is too thick. Stir in the sugar and the cooked chicken pieces. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the gravy.
7.  **Finish with Cream and Butter:** Crush the kasuri methi between your palms to release its aroma and stir it into the gravy. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Cook for just 1-2 minutes more, ensuring not to boil after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

## Tips for the Perfect Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken Recipe at home is entirely possible with a few insider tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt and spices tenderize the chicken and infuse it with deep flavor, which is crucial for the final dish.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is non-negotiable for the signature creamy texture. Straining it afterwards takes it to the next level.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Tomatoes can be quite acidic. A touch of sugar (or even honey) helps balance this acidity, bringing out the sweetness and richness of the other ingredients.
*   **Kasuri Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is a secret weapon in Butter Chicken. It provides a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is distinctive to Murgh Makhani. Gently toasting it in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing enhances its aroma.
*   **Don't Boil After Cream:** Adding cream at the very end and only gently warming it through prevents it from splitting or curdling, maintaining the gravy's luxurious texture.
*   **Good Quality Butter/Ghee:** Since butter is in the name, using high-quality butter or ghee will significantly impact the flavor profile.

## Serving Your Murgh Makhani

Once your Murgh Makhani is ready, the serving presentation adds to the experience. Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves and a swirl of extra heavy cream for a visually appealing finish. This rich and flavorful dish pairs perfectly with:

*   **Naan Bread:** Especially garlic naan or butter naan, which are perfect for scooping up every last bit of that delectable gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps soak up the sauce.
*   **A Simple Salad:** A light side salad of sliced cucumbers, onions, and tomatoes can offer a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.

## Butter Chicken Variations & FAQs

This classic Butter Chicken Recipe is a fantastic starting point, but there are always questions and possibilities for variation.

**Q: Can I make it spicier?**
A: Absolutely! Increase the amount of red chili powder in both the marinade and the gravy, or add a finely chopped green chili to the gravy base.

**Q: What if I don't have cashews?**
A: Cashews provide richness and thickening. You can substitute them with blanched almonds (soaked and peeled), or for a nut-free option, use a tablespoon of poppy seeds or just rely on the cream for richness.

**Q: Can I make this vegetarian or vegan?**
A: Yes! For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or chickpeas. For a vegan Butter Chicken Recipe, replace dairy yogurt with a plant-based alternative, use oil instead of ghee/butter, and substitute heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or a cashew cream.

**Q: Does Butter Chicken freeze well?**
A: The gravy freezes exceptionally well. You can make a large batch of the gravy and freeze portions. When ready to eat, thaw, reheat, add your cooked chicken, and finish with cream and butter.

**Q: What is Kashmiri red chili powder?**
A: Kashmiri chili powder is a milder chili powder known for imparting a vibrant red color without excessive heat, making it ideal for dishes like Butter Chicken where color is desired. If unavailable, use regular red chili powder sparingly.

Creating your own Butter Chicken from scratch is an incredibly rewarding experience. The aroma alone will transport you, and the taste will leave you wondering why you ever ordered takeout. This detailed Butter Chicken Recipe empowers you to bring the magic of Murgh Makhani into your home kitchen. Enjoy the process, savor the flavors, and delight in sharing this beloved Indian classic with your loved ones.
